short: Bell-basis parity for controlled spin swaps

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.BellAsymCore.cleanRealizesSet_bellFiveStepNoNegCoreSliceDyn_asym
lean.plain: Two clean SELECT calls with shared Bell parity
lean.annotation: `hTurnSupp` excludes the system wires and the wire holding the Bell parity. The intervening circuit can change the spin control, so the second controlled Z uses that control and the stored parity. An X-basis measurement erases the parity with a phase corrected by Clifford gates on the transformed pairs.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.SevenGearWalk333.fast7gSevenGearCert
lean.plain: Walk blocks at the scheduled workspace widths
lean.annotation: The certificate checks the scheduled implementations. Within a block the circuit shares Bell parity between SELECT calls and across adjacent steps. The accounting charges $464K+232$ T gates for spin swaps in a $K$-step block, including the ordinary endpoint swaps. The $K-1$ intervening reflections add 84 T gates each.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.BellAsymCore.cleanRealizesSet_bellFiveStepNoNegCoreSliceDyn_asym
lean.plain: Two clean SELECT calls with shared Bell parity
lean.annotation: The swap multiplies the antisymmetric Bell state by −1 and fixes the three symmetric Bell states. A CNOT and a Hadamard send the antisymmetric state to $|11\rangle$. Computing the parity of such pairs and applying a controlled Z implements the block of controlled swaps. The Lean statement verifies the clean composition of two SELECT calls with an intervening reflection.

statements.markdown: each block can instead be implemented as a single controlled sign flip
